notes:
Jaguar I-PACE (X590, 2018 to 2024) on the OBD socket's ISO 15765-4 CAN, 11-bit identifiers at 500 kbit/s, with UDS.

The units come from two open sources, recorded with their limits in docs/vehicles/europe-other.md: OBDb's Jaguar-I-PACE repository (CC-BY-SA-4.0; its signalset and its per-model-year response records, taking only the request header and service) and the Open Vehicle Monitoring System's vehicle_jaguaripace module (MIT; ipace_obd_pids.h names the modules and vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp polls some of them). Neither is a Jaguar document. Only the units both sources place at the same address are in the profile: the battery energy control module, HVAC, tyre pressure and telematics units, which both read with service 22, and the powertrain, gear shift and charger units, which OBDb's records show answering and OVMS names without polling. The reply is the request plus 8: OVMS polls each unit on its identifier with bit 0x8 set, and OBDb gives no other response header.

Left out: the other units named only in ipace_obd_pids.h (among them the body control and gateway module at 0x726, which OVMS polls for the vehicle speed, the brake booster at 0x7E2, the ABS at 0x7E6, the inverters at 0x746 and 0x747 and the DC to DC converter at 0x753), because no second source places them. The two sources also disagree on which unit answers the speed (OBDb 0x7E4, OVMS 0x726) and the cabin temperature (OBDb 0x733, OVMS 0x7E4) identifiers; the profile carries no identifiers, only the units.

Neither source opens a session, so the profile uses the UDS default session, and neither reads fault codes, so service 19 on these units is untested by any source. A tool vendor lists DoIP support for the I-PACE (a search summary only, in the same document); that does not say whether the CAN pins carry these units, and OBDb's records show that they answered there. Treat every row as unconfirmed until obd-read probe shows the unit answering.
name: jaguar-i-pace

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.

powertrain.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x7E0 answered the legislated service 01 requests in every model-year record (2019, 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024); the signalset has no service 22 command for it; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x7E0 named the Powertrain Control Module, which OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp) does not poll, so the reply rests on OVMS's rule of the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. No source shows this unit answering service 22 or 19. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.

gear-shift.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE signalset (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145404/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json) and OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x732 with service 22 (a parked-state signal), answered in the 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023 records; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x732 named the Gear Shift Control Module, which OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp) does not poll, so the reply rests on OVMS's rule of the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.

hvac.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE signalset (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145404/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json) and OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x733 with service 22 (ambient and cabin temperature signals), answered in the 2019 and 2020 records and refused for the ambient temperature identifier in the 2021 and 2023 records; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x733 named the HVAC Control Module; OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp): polls it with service 22 for the ambient temperature, with the reply on the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.

tpms.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE signalset (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145404/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json) and OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x751 with service 22 (tyre pressure and temperature signals), answered in the 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023 records; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x751 named the Tire pressure Monitoring System; OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp): polls it with service 22 for the four tyre pressures and temperatures, with the reply on the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.

telematics.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE signalset (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145404/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json) and OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x754 with service 22 (a GPS satellite count signal), answered in the 2020 record only; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x754 named the Telematics Control Module; OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp): polls it with service 22 for the localisation identifier, with the reply on the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.

battery-energy.source: OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE signalset (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145404/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json) and OBDb Jaguar-I-PACE response records (https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145418/https://github.com/OBDb/Jaguar-I-PACE/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2020/command_support.yaml, and the files for the other model years beside it): 0x7E4 with service 22 (cell voltage, pack voltage, current, temperature, state of charge and state of health signals), answered in the 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023 records; OVMS ipace_obd_pids.h (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145437/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/ipace_obd_pids.h): 0x7E4 named the Battery Energy Control Module; OVMS vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp (https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp, snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20261116145630/https://github.com/openvehicles/Open-Vehicle-Monitoring-System-3/blob/master/vehicle/OVMS.V3/components/vehicle_jaguaripace/src/vehicle_jaguaripace.cpp): polls it with service 22 for the battery state of charge, state of health, voltages and temperatures, with the reply on the request identifier with bit 0x8 set. Two sources agree on the address. Not read from a car.
